GREENPODS DISASTERS

By: Nicky Troll | Delivery

Proposal


Show: Carte Blanche

One Liner (Tonight on Carte Blanche...):
We expose a Green Modular Home Designer that sets out to build dream homes only to deliver structures that get condemned & demolished - leaving you out of pocket and homeless.

Unique Selling Point:
Classic crook!
Our viewers are the victims
Big money
Visual evidence
Opportunity for a lekker confront

Summary:
Imagine building your dream house, that’s innovative & kind to the environment. Erwin van der Weerd is the designer engineer that will sell you the chance to make your dream a reality with his stunning modular pod homes.

It's a very quick, cost-effective way of creating an energy saving, low maintenance home.

Well, that’s if you get it…and if you do, one thing it’s often not – is SAFE! The structures don’t meet building regulations and don’t get signed off – declaring your innovative new home un-liveable.

We exposed the man behind these disaster homes.

Further information:
WHAT THEY SELL
Greenpods™ produce beautiful modular pod homes between 15m2 upwards. These can be stand-alone or a combination of pods. It's the perfect option for a starter home, granny cottage, modular school building, mobile classrooms, meeting rooms, security offices, therapy rooms, B&B, office, gym, art or writing studio, guest cottage or even A-frame wooden tents for game farms. It's a very quick, cost-effective way of creating an energy saving, low maintenance home. We have existing plans and a choice of finishes to meet your budget, our bedrooms, bathrooms and kitchens, come complete with fancy pants fittings and fixtures. Even the foundation is included in the price!

ACCEPT THE FOUNDATION ARE SHAKY….

WHO IS GREENPODS
The brain behind the operation is Erwin van der Weerd. He used to own Perfect-Places but the company started getting a bad reputation and his girlfriend, Tracey Dollman, is now the front for Greenpods. In the Greenpods contracts, it states that Perfect-Places will do the building. Also when I called the landline – the person that answered said Tracey was the marketing director and Erwin was the technical director.

Erwin starts off as a charming and confident designer and engineer – he then turns into an arrogant psychopath according his long list of unhappy clients.

WHAT’s THE ISSUE?
These unit can cost anything from R320 000 up to just under R2 million. Because it’s pre-manufactured, the company charges 85% up front. The balance when they come and assemble it on your plot.

I have a list of at least 7 clients that have had huge structural issues that resulted in them having to either bring in third party builders to rectify the problems before getting engineers to sign off and issue certificates to occupy OR worst case scenario the structures had to be demolished completely. I know of at least two units that were condemned and demolished.

It’s a combination of design flaws, shoddy workmanship & quality of materials used.

WHAT’s THE DEAL WITH THE REGULATIONS
Timber frame construction is regulated by the SABS and S400 (National Building Regulations) – technically if these regulations are followed an engineer sign off is not needed. Erwin is from Holland and has brought his concept to SA without adapting his processes according to our climatic conditions.

The problem is that it isn’t anyone’s responsibility to control the implementation of these standards – the NHBRC assists and protects housing consumers who have been exposed to contractors who deliver housing units of substandard design, workmanship and poor quality material. The NHBRC has been involved with number of Erwin’s disaster projects. BUT they don’t actually control the implementation of the standards and regulations…. NO ONE DOES…. Leaving the door wide open to chancers.

INDUSTRY BODIES
There are two relevant industry bodies: The Institute for Timber Construction & The Timber Frame Builders Association of South Africa. But these are voluntary bodies and in reality have no teeth.

THE CASE STUDIES

1. Robbie Alexander – DEVELOPER – 0829047413
robbie@alexbro.com

Ordered 6 units in Stellenbosch – got two that were defective, four outstanding – has taken civil and criminal action. Has multiple reports.

2. Lorraine & Ewald Boshoff – Riebeek Kasteel – 082 835 5401
ewaldboshoff1@gmail.com, lorraineirene@gmail.com
House was demolished – put R1 million of their retirement money in – kids helped by taking loans to build brick & mortar house. Has report from the Institute for Timber Construction.

3. Robbie Cameron-Franschhoek - 083 229 1380 - robbie@rca.co.za
Marco Fouche…building inspector for Franshoek condemned house - 021 808 8329 / 082 474 4140
House was demolished – lost around R2 million – have the reports and contacts for the Municipal inspector that condemned the building. Has report from the NHBRC.

4. Mano-Houtbay – Architect that commissioned Erwin to do it – says it was a disaster – had to get in other company to finish it. Is frustrated by the lack of power industry bodies have because Erwin continues to build disasters.
079 708 1120

5. Eleonora Engelbrecht – 0723610724 – NEWEST victim – currently trying to finish construction – but no join – engineer won’t sign off saying it’s not safe. Has extensive snag list and photographs.

UNDERCOVER
We set up a sting to meet Erwin about a potential project. A PI will meet with him posing as my boyfriend to get the initial hidden camera footage of his sales pitch.

FOR THE BUST - we have a home address, a factory address and we'll try to create a reason for another meeting.

EXPERT
Horton Hunter of Henton Homes (timber frame builder that had a look at house in Riebeck Kasteel) : 083 268 4609

SUPPLIERS NOT PAID
1. Zaida Davids …076 401 9120
They got a court judgement against Erwin, and he has not honoured monthly payments since October 2017

CAPE TOWN TRIP. THE WHOLE STORY IS THERE.I might need an extra half day to cover travel - the case studies are about an hour and half outside of CPT

Script:


STRUCTURE

VO: The world is moving towards greener living – with people making lifestyle choices that are not only sustainable but also kind to the environment.

LINK: So the idea of living in a green, energy saving, low maintenance home that is also quick & cost-effective to build is becoming an even more attractive option for South Africans looking to build their dream homes.

VO: That’s exactly what Eleonora Engelbrecht had mind for her plot in Simonstown.

ELEONORA: I wanted // something that was green, I like timber // that’s why I went with the Greenpods home

VO: They weren’t the cheapest – so Eleonora expected quality from the Cape Town based company – Greenpods. They offer a turn-key modular timber home solution, that incorporates design, construction, fittings and fixtures.

The brain behind the designs is Dutch born Erwin van der Weerd – he formerly owned Perfect-Places but is now the technical director of the company owned by Tracey Dollman.

In Eleonora’s contract Erwin’s company Perfect Places is listed as the sub contractor.

LINK: This is a modern twist to a traditional timber house that looks great from the outside. But looks can be deceiving - structurally this house is unsafe and should not be occupied.

ELEONORA: You don’t want it, you don’t want this nightmare – you don’t want this hassle – my husband and I have been struggling with this for over a year. INT3 M4 // At the end of the day the structure is not safe.

VO: Eleonora paid Greenpods 90% of the total amount by the end of March 2017, but still doesn’t have a complete home. Her snag lists includes major structural issues.

ELEONORA: Erwin keeps saying – no, this is all right, there’s nothing wrong,
DEVI: Did an engineer sign off on this house?
ELEONORA: yes, an engineer signed off on this house….

VO: That is highly unusual and should never have happened - we decided to pay engineer, Ishaq Ebrahim and his son, Mahir, a visit.

MAHIR: The problem was there were certain things that needed to be fixed and when I spoke with Erwin he agreed that the would fix those things – so then I filled in the completion certificate on condition that those things would be completed.
DEVI: Is that how it works?
ISAQ: It was purely on trust – I don’t know what to say to you any more – we don’t do that – we’ve been in business for many many years.

VO: While they later retracted the completion certificate for Eleonora’s house – they say they deeply regret the initial sign off.

ISAQ: I never came across anything like this in my life when I saw what was done there – //

LINK: The design is not the problem – it is innovative and eco-friendly – the plans get approved by council and are structurally sound on paper – the issue is the execution and workmanship.

VO: We met Stefan Janser from the National Home Builders Registration Council , or NHBRC at Eleonora’s home for a site inspection.

STEFAN: Generally all around here we are finding that the fixing details of the substructure to the house is where there are problems

VO: Brackets were not fixed properly, what appears to be structural posts are randomly positioned and don’t even touch the base of the house, beams were spliced incorrectly and not supported structurally.

And in some places pieces of wood were simply shoved into the gaps.

DEVI” Not supposed to have this?
STEAFN: – you should not have a gap and they’ve used a wedging piece here to just to level up this whole beam over the post – which is incorrect.

LINK: Erwin van Weerd blames everybody - he blames his clients, the weather, the NHBRC, pesky building regulations and even his own contractors for the workmanship – I think it’s time he takes some responsibility.




VO: We went to the factory in Cape Town – where he and Tracy work from.

DEVI: you don’t take responsibility
ERWIN: that’s their story
DEVI: do you?
ERWIN I do
DEVI: I can’t hear you taking responsibility for Eleonora’s house
ERWIN: why – we built fantastic house
DEVI: no it’s not!
ERWIN: it is a stunning house
DEVI: your opinions are problematic – it’s structural not sound
ERWIN: that’swhere I disagree
DEVI: nhbrc – they are experts
ERWIN: they sign off when engineer signs off
DEVI: he withdrew his signature
ERWIN: said need more bracing

VO: Erwin is referring to this brace - where a single screw was used and completely missed the post.

DEVI: you haven’t done all the work
ERWIN did the work requested
DEVI: when? Between last night till the morning – did you do it? Because last night I was there.
ERWIN: No, no, no, no…

VO: We asked him about using random of pieces of wood to fill in gaps.

DEVI: The NHBRC //want to know in what world can you just wedge it in with a piece of wood that was just hanging around there?
ERWIN: But this has nothing to do with structural / nothing to do with structural connection
DEVI: They say it is.
ERWIN: No it isn’t
DEVI: Do the nhbrc know what they are talking about?
ERWIN: With wood frame sometimes I doubt it.

VO: But this wasn’t the first time Erwin’s work had been called into the question by the NHBRC.

In 2015, retired couple Ewald & Lorraine Boshoff relocated to Riebeeck Kasteel in the Western Cape. By the end of June 2016, they had paid Erwin’s Company Perfect-Places, just close to one million rand to build their dream home.

DEVI: When did he finish the house?
EWALD: He never finished the house. I got about 40% of a house – because it deteriorated so badly after those month that the NHBRC has stopped him

VO: The NHBRC stopped construction sighting major structural non-compliance issues.

STEFAN: We had problems in terms of the connectivity, the connections, the lintels, the over beams – a whole lot of technical and structural issues that we were concerned about.

VO: Erwin is of the opinion that these were minor issues.

DEVI: The NHBRC found 10 issues that were non compliant – did you fix it
ERWIN: Yes, there was a whole list – we made a whole report – there was something like a 10 / 15 page document that was sent back to them – explaining how it works and how we calculated it.

VO: He may have calculated it but not all the suggested remedies were approved by the NHBRC.

STEFAN: We had tremendous engagement with the homebuilder and his engineer to say this is what needs to be done but in this particular case it seemed like there was a reluctance to meet those requirements.

VO: And while the Boshoffs waited, the structure was exposed to weather conditions causing serious damage to the structural integrity and giving rise to black mould on the surfaces.

After months of no progress – they cancelled the contract with Erwin.

And with no other timber company willing to take on the structural risk of the project - the Boshoffs had no choice but to demolish Erwin van der Weerd’s million rand structure.

They then forked out an extra million rand for a new contractor to build a brick and mortar house.

DEVI: how affect retirement plan?
EWALD: it wiped out everything // We would have been out on the street basically if it wasn’t for our children sourcing funds through loans to help us out.

VO: Erwin claimed it was news to him that the structure had been demolished.

DEVI: They built a brand new house on top of those foundations
ERWIN: on those foundations?
DEVI: The house they paid you a million rand for is not there – they’ve only got the foundations – I’d be a bit upset
ERWIN: I’d be upset…
DEVI: They say this drama too much for them they blame you
ERWIN: I can imagine
dEvI: you don’t think they are blaming you fairly?
ERWIN: no, I don’t think so no –
DEVI: not your fault
ERWIN: // the major issue was that the NHBRC didn’t understand how we build modular timber houses

VO: Janser says this is ludicrous.

STEFAN: We don’t have a problem with modular systems // this isn’t even innovative // it’s a timber frame structure // I can categorically state that the building work // did not meet the standards and the NHBRC was doing it’s job.

VO: In some cases it went beyond the quality of work.

In 2016, Six pods were ordered for a Stellenbosch Development at a price tag of just under R6 million – again Erwin’s Company was the sub-contractor and point of contact. They only received four!

Company representative Ilzemarie Knoetze says maybe it was a blessing in disguise.

ILZEMARIE: The first two pods started to go skew – you could actually see the pod going to the side and the roof of the pods were also doing this.
DEVI: And then?
ILZEMARIE: it just got from bad to worse // we had two pods 85 % completed, we had two pods that was 20% completed and for the other two pods –for 1.7 million worth of money– we had nothing.

VO: Erwin denies these allegations – he says they only paid for four pods - which were delivered.

DEVI: so where is the other two pods?
ERWIBNN: He didn’t pay the full amount – 4.5 – there were two pods outstanding.

VO: Ilzemarie’s documentation proves otherwise – she says the company is not going to leave matter there.

ILZEMARIE: We’ve laid a criminal charge for the 1.7 million for the two pods that we received nothing for.

VO: The NHBRC says Erwin’s transgressions go beyond shoddy workmanship – he is currently not registered as a home builder with the council.

STEFAN: Erwin at this particular point and time is suspended with the NHBRC //he cannot trade or enrol any houses.

VO: Erwin claimed his registration simply lapsed…

DEVI: The NHBRC said they suspended your licence
ERWIN: No I am not aware of that. //INT1 M57

VO: He was sent the notice of suspension, in writing, by registered mail.

He currently is operating in contravention of the Housing Consumers Protection Measures Act making Builder registration and the enrolment of new homes with the NHBRC a statutory requirement.

DEVI: How many have you done?
ERWIN: about 20 or so
DEVI: how many did you register with the NHBRC?
ERWIN 3 or 4 or 5 – 6 or 7 yah…
DEVI: three are registered –
ERWIN: before it became compulsory….

VO: No Erwin, It’s been compulsory since 1998 when the act was promulgated.

Essentially all the new houses he has built over last couple of years, are illegal structures - except for the three he did enrolled – two of which were demolished.

While the Boshoffs house is long gone – Ewald says his experience with Erwin van der Weerd still haunts him.

EWALD: I don’t know if I’ll ever have peace of mind – but no person deserves – never mind the age or the circumstances to go through that process again.












PROMOS

PROMO 1
VO: We expose a timber home builder offering green homes only to deliver structures that are not legal & structurally unsound - leaving you out of pocket and homeless.

PROMO 2
VO: While this modern timber home may look great from the outside - looks can be deceiving.

ELEONORA: You don’t want it, you don’t want this nightmare // the structure is not safe.

VO: We expose a timber home builder’s dodgy workmanship.

PROMO 3
VO: Imagine building a dream home that’s not only innovative but also kind to the environment, only to find out it’s not safe to live in.

STEFAN: // I can categorically state that the building work // did not meet the standards // INT4 M15

VO: We expose the man behind these shaky designs.

VO: We went to the factory in Cape Town – where he and Tracy work from. DEVI: you don’t take responsibility ERWIN: that’s their story DEVI: do you? ERWIN I do DEVI: I can’t hear you taking responsibility for Eleonora’s house ERWIN: why – we built fantastic house DEVI: no it’s not! ERWIN: it is a stunning house DEVI: your opinions are problematic – it’s structural not sound ERWIN: that’swhere I disagree DEVI: nhbrc – they are experts ERWIN: they sign off when engineer signs off DEVI: he withdrew his signature ERWIN: said need more bracing VO: Erwin is referring to this brace - where a single screw was used and completely missed the post. DEVI: you haven’t done all the work ERWIN did the work requested DEVI: when? Between last night till the morning – did you do it? Because last night I was there. ERWIN: No, no, no, no… VO: We asked him about using random of pieces of wood to fill in gaps. DEVI: The NHBRC //want to know in what world can you just wedge it in with a piece of wood that was just hanging around there? ERWIN: But this has nothing to do with structural / nothing to do with structural connection DEVI: They say it is. ERWIN: No it isn’t DEVI: Do the nhbrc know what they are talking about? ERWIN: With wood frame sometimes I doubt it. VO: But this wasn’t the first time Erwin’s work had been called into the question by the NHBRC. In 2015, retired couple Ewald & Lorraine Boshoff relocated to Riebeeck Kasteel in the Western Cape. By the end of June 2016, they had paid Erwin’s Company Perfect-Places, just close to one million rand to build their dream home. DEVI: When did he finish the house? EWALD: He never finished the house. I got about 40% of a house – because it deteriorated so badly after those month that the NHBRC has stopped him VO: The NHBRC stopped construction sighting major structural non-compliance issues. STEFAN: We had problems in terms of the connectivity, the connections, the lintels, the over beams – a whole lot of technical and structural issues that we were concerned about. VO: Erwin is of the opinion that these were minor issues. DEVI: The NHBRC found 10 issues that were non compliant – did you fix it ERWIN: Yes, there was a whole list – we made a whole report – there was something like a 10 / 15 page document that was sent back to them – explaining how it works and how we calculated it. VO: He may have calculated it but not all the suggested remedies were approved by the NHBRC. STEFAN: We had tremendous engagement with the homebuilder and his engineer to say this is what needs to be done but in this particular case it seemed like there was a reluctance to meet those requirements. VO: And while the Boshoffs waited, the structure was exposed to weather conditions causing serious damage to the structural integrity and giving rise to black mould on the surfaces. After months of no progress – they cancelled the contract with Erwin. And with no other timber company willing to take on the structural risk of the project - the Boshoffs had no choice but to demolish Erwin van der Weerd’s million rand structure. They then forked out an extra million rand for a new contractor to build a brick and mortar house. DEVI: how affect retirement plan? EWALD: it wiped out everything // We would have been out on the street basically if it wasn’t for our children sourcing funds through loans to help us out. VO: Erwin claimed it was news to him that the structure had been demolished. DEVI: They built a brand new house on top of those foundations ERWIN: on those foundations? DEVI: The house they paid you a million rand for is not there – they’ve only got the foundations – I’d be a bit upset ERWIN: I’d be upset… DEVI: They say this drama too much for them they blame you ERWIN: I can imagine dEvI: you don’t think they are blaming you fairly? ERWIN: no, I don’t think so no – DEVI: not your fault ERWIN: // the major issue was that the NHBRC didn’t understand how we build modular timber houses VO: Janser says this is ludicrous. STEFAN: We don’t have a problem with modular systems // this isn’t even innovative // it’s a timber frame structure // I can categorically state that the building work // did not meet the standards and the NHBRC was doing it’s job. VO: In some cases it went beyond the quality of work. In 2016, Six pods were ordered for a Stellenbosch Development at a price tag of just under R6 million – again Erwin’s Company was the sub-contractor and point of contact. They only received four! Company representative Ilzemarie Knoetze says maybe it was a blessing in disguise. ILZEMARIE: The first two pods started to go skew – you could actually see the pod going to the side and the roof of the pods were also doing this. DEVI: And then? ILZEMARIE: it just got from bad to worse // we had two pods 85 % completed, we had two pods that was 20% completed and for the other two pods –for 1.7 million worth of money– we had nothing. VO: Erwin denies these allegations – he says they only paid for four pods - which were delivered. DEVI: so where is the other two pods? ERWIBNN: He didn’t pay the full amount – 4.5 – there were two pods outstanding. VO: Ilzemarie’s documentation proves otherwise – she says the company is not going to leave matter there. ILZEMARIE: We’ve laid a criminal charge for the 1.7 million for the two pods that we received nothing for. VO: The NHBRC says Erwin’s transgressions go beyond shoddy workmanship – he is currently not registered as a home builder with the council. STEFAN: Erwin at this particular point and time is suspended with the NHBRC //he cannot trade or enrol any houses. VO: Erwin claimed his registration simply lapsed… DEVI: The NHBRC said they suspended your licence ERWIN: No I am not aware of that. //INT1 M57 VO: He was sent the notice of suspension, in writing, by registered mail. He currently is operating in contravention of the Housing Consumers Protection Measures Act making Builder registration and the enrolment of new homes with the NHBRC a statutory requirement. DEVI: How many have you done? ERWIN: about 20 or so DEVI: how many did you register with the NHBRC? ERWIN 3 or 4 or 5 – 6 or 7 yah… DEVI: three are registered – ERWIN: before it became compulsory…. VO: No Erwin, It’s been compulsory since 1998 when the act was promulgated. Essentially all the new houses he has built over last couple of years, are illegal structures - except for the three he did enrolled – two of which were demolished. While the Boshoffs house is long gone – Ewald says his experience with Erwin van der Weerd still haunts him. EWALD: I don’t know if I’ll ever have peace of mind – but no person deserves – never mind the age or the circumstances to go through that process again. PROMO 2 VO: While this modern timber home may look great from the outside - looks can be deceiving. ELEONORA: You don’t want it, you don’t want this nightmare // the structure is not safe. VO: We expose a timber home builder’s dodgy workmanship. PROMO 3 VO: Imagine building a dream home that’s not only innovative but also kind to the environment, only to find out it’s not safe to live in. metadata.Summary: Imagine building your dream house, that’s innovative & kind to the environment. Erwin van der Weerd is the designer engineer that will sell you the chance to make your dream a reality with his stunning modular pod homes. It's a very quick, cost-effective way of creating an energy saving, low maintenance home. Well, that’s if you get it…and if you do, one thing it’s often not – is SAFE! The structures don’t meet building regulations and don’t get signed off – declaring your innovative new home un-liveable. We exposed the man behind these disaster homes.
metadata.Further information: WHAT THEY SELL Greenpods™ produce beautiful modular pod homes between 15m2 upwards. These can be stand-alone or a combination of pods. It's the perfect option for a starter home, granny cottage, modular school building, mobile classrooms, meeting rooms, security offices, therapy rooms, B&B, office, gym, art or writing studio, guest cottage or even A-frame wooden tents for game farms. It's a very quick, cost-effective way of creating an energy saving, low maintenance home. We have existing plans and a choice of finishes to meet your budget, our bedrooms, bathrooms and kitchens, come complete with fancy pants fittings and fixtures. Even the foundation is included in the price! ACCEPT THE FOUNDATION ARE SHAKY…. WHO IS GREENPODS The brain behind the operation is Erwin van der Weerd. He used to own Perfect-Places but the company started getting a bad reputation and his girlfriend, Tracey Dollman, is now the front for Greenpods. In the Greenpods contracts, it states that Perfect-Places will do the building. Also when I called the landline – the person that answered said Tracey was the marketing director and Erwin was the technical director. Erwin starts off as a charming and confident designer and engineer – he then turns into an arrogant psychopath according his long list of unhappy clients. WHAT’s THE ISSUE? These unit can cost anything from R320 000 up to just under R2 million. Because it’s pre-manufactured, the company charges 85% up front. The balance when they come and assemble it on your plot. I have a list of at least 7 clients that have had huge structural issues that resulted in them having to either bring in third party builders to rectify the problems before getting engineers to sign off and issue certificates to occupy OR worst case scenario the structures had to be demolished completely. I know of at least two units that were condemned and demolished. It’s a combination of design flaws, shoddy workmanship & quality of materials used. WHAT’s THE DEAL WITH THE REGULATIONS Timber frame construction is regulated by the SABS and S400 (National Building Regulations) – technically if these regulations are followed an engineer sign off is not needed. Erwin is from Holland and has brought his concept to SA without adapting his processes according to our climatic conditions. The problem is that it isn’t anyone’s responsibility to control the implementation of these standards – the NHBRC assists and protects housing consumers who have been exposed to contractors who deliver housing units of substandard design, workmanship and poor quality material. The NHBRC has been involved with number of Erwin’s disaster projects. BUT they don’t actually control the implementation of the standards and regulations…. NO ONE DOES…. Leaving the door wide open to chancers. INDUSTRY BODIES There are two relevant industry bodies: The Institute for Timber Construction & The Timber Frame Builders Association of South Africa. But these are voluntary bodies and in reality have no teeth. THE CASE STUDIES 1. Robbie Alexander – DEVELOPER – 0829047413 robbie@alexbro.com Ordered 6 units in Stellenbosch – got two that were defective, four outstanding – has taken civil and criminal action. Has multiple reports. 2. Lorraine & Ewald Boshoff – Riebeek Kasteel – 082 835 5401 ewaldboshoff1@gmail.com, lorraineirene@gmail.com House was demolished – put R1 million of their retirement money in – kids helped by taking loans to build brick & mortar house. Has report from the Institute for Timber Construction. 3. Robbie Cameron-Franschhoek - 083 229 1380 - robbie@rca.co.za Marco Fouche…building inspector for Franshoek condemned house - 021 808 8329 / 082 474 4140 House was demolished – lost around R2 million – have the reports and contacts for the Municipal inspector that condemned the building. Has report from the NHBRC. 4. Mano-Houtbay – Architect that commissioned Erwin to do it – says it was a disaster – had to get in other company to finish it. Is frustrated by the lack of power industry bodies have because Erwin continues to build disasters. 079 708 1120 5. Eleonora Engelbrecht – 0723610724 – NEWEST victim – currently trying to finish construction – but no join – engineer won’t sign off saying it’s not safe. Has extensive snag list and photographs. FOR THE BUST - we have a home address, a factory address and we'll try to create a reason for another meeting.
